rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this verse, poverty is the actual present cause of infanticide; elsewhere the Quran also forbids killing children from fear of future poverty, and Arabs buried daughters through inability or anticipation.
rows.anchor: والإملاق : الفقر ، وكونه علة لقتل الأولاد يقع على وجهين : أن يكون حاصلا بالفعل ، وهو المراد هنا

rows.speaker: إسحاق بن خلف
rows.claim: His poem depicts a father dreading that poverty will expose his daughter's body to hardship, illustrating fear of future poverty as a motive for infanticide.
rows.anchor:
قال إسحاق بن خلف ، وهو إسلامي قديم :
إذا تذكرت بنتي حين تندبني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of provision interrupts the prohibition and refutes poverty as an excuse: God provided for children, so a father should earn for them rather than kill them.
rows.anchor: علة للنهي عن قتلهم ، إبطالا لمعذرتهم : لأن الفقر قد جعلوه عذرا لقتل الأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speech shifts from speaking of the Lord in the third person to God's first-person voice, making God seem to speak directly and confirming the Messenger.
rows.anchor: إلى طريق التكلم بضمير : نرزقكم تذكيرا بالذي أمر بهذا القول كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parents are mentioned before their children because God has sustained the parents without their starving; poverty afflicted the parents, not the children.
rows.anchor: وقدم رزق الآباء للإشارة إلى أنه كما رزق الآباء ، فلم يموتوا جوعا ، كذلك يرزق الأبناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the subject in the provision clause conveys exclusivity: God provides for parents and children, while parents provide for neither themselves nor their children.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المسند إليه على المسند الفعلي . هنا لإفادة الاختصاص : أي نحن نرزقكم وإياهم لا أنتم ترزقون أنفسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition against approaching indecencies warns more forcefully than forbidding their commission; proximity implies even slight involvement, a metaphorical extension because sins have no literal location.
rows.anchor: وقد نهى عن القرب منها ، وهو أبلغ في التحذير من النهي عن ملابستها : لأن القرب من الشيء مظنة الوقوع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Indecencies are major sins involving harmful consequences; public examples include anger and slander, while hidden examples chiefly include adultery and theft, common among Arabs.
rows.anchor: والفواحش : الآثام الكبيرة ، وهي المشتملة على مفاسد

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: He interprets indecencies specifically as adultery: public sexual acts in brothels and private illicit lovers as the hidden form.
rows.anchor: ومن المفسرين من فسر الفواحش بالزنا ، وجعل ما ظهر منها ما يفعله سفهاؤهم في الحوانيت وديار البغايا ، وبما بطن اتخاذ الأخدان سرا ، وروي هذا عن السدي

rows.speaker: الضحاك وابن عباس
rows.claim: They report that pre-Islamic Arabs treated secret adultery as permissible but disapproved of it publicly, so God prohibited both forms.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الضحاك وابن عباس : كان أهل الجاهلية يرون الزنا سرا حلالا ، ويستقبحونه في العلانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural indecencies favors the broad meaning of major sins; the similar list in al-Isra does not require both passages to mean only adultery.
rows.anchor: وعندي أن صيغة الجمع في الفواحش ترجح التفسير الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distinction between what is apparent and concealed was explained earlier in the same surah.
rows.anchor: وتقدم القول في : { ما ظهر منها وما بطن } عند قوله تعالى : { وذروا ظاهر الإثم وباطنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Killing is singled out as a grave, widespread indecency under the broad interpretation; the generic definite soul encompasses all persons.
rows.anchor: وأعقب ذلك بالنهي عن قتل النفس ، وهو من الفواحش على تفسيرها بالأعم ، تخصيصا له بالذكر : لأنه فساد عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing the soul as forbidden emphasizes that its prohibition is ancient, dating from Adam; attaching prohibition to a person means prohibition of killing that person.
rows.anchor: تأكيدا للتحريم بأنه تحريم قديم فإن الله حرم قتل النفس من عهد آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the wording may mean God made the soul inviolable; the author cites the sacred precinct and a hadith about what lies between Medina's lava fields.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون معنى : { حرم الله } جعلها الله حرما أي شيئا محترما لا يعتدى عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception covers every circumstance of killing: no killing is allowed except for a cause established as rightful under sound reason and the relevant law; the preposition marks circumstance or cause.
rows.anchor: استثناء مفرغ من عموم أحوال ملابسة القتل ، أي لا تقتلوها في أية حالة أو بأي سبب تنتحلونه إلا بسبب الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Islamic usage, rightful killing includes combatants and retaliation established by the Quran, plus apostasy after seeking repentance, adultery by a married person, and persistent refusal of prayer after its time, based on hadiths.
rows.anchor: وقد فصل الإسلام حق قتل النفس بالقرآن والسنة ، وهو قتل المحارب والقصاص ، وهذان بنص القرآن ، وقتل المرتد عن الإسلام بعد استتابته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other lawful cases include killing in authorized defense, rebels and zakat-refusers; jihad itself is outside this exception, though killing a prisoner for a valid interest can be rightful.
rows.anchor: فيه شرعا وذلك قتل من يقتل من البغاة وهو بنص القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular demonstrative refers collectively to all the preceding commands; a plural demonstrative would also be idiomatic.
rows.anchor: والإشارة بقوله : { ذلكم وصاكم به } إلى مجموع ما ذكر ، ولذلك أفرد اسم الإشارة باعتبار المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wish that people reason means they should become rational: committing these prohibitions shows such debased judgment that offenders seem mindless.
rows.anchor: أي يصيروا ذوي عقول لأن ملابسة بعض هذه المحرمات ينبىء عن خساسة عقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing sentence marks the end of prohibitions concerned with social order: right belief, family stability, avoiding corruption, and preserving life by ending mutual killing.
rows.anchor: فأومأ إلى تنهية نوع من المحرمات وهو المحرمات الراجع تحريمها إلى إصلاح الحالة الاجتماعية للأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This group of prohibitions protects human dealings, builds the Muslim community and its civic order, and establishes mutual trust; it begins with the vulnerable orphan who cannot defend property rights.
rows.anchor: عطف محرمات ترجع إلى حفظ قواع التعامل بين الناس لإقامة قواعد الجامعة الإسلامية ومدنيتها وتحقيق ثقة الناس بعضهم ببعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Approaching an orphan's property means dealing with it; the exception allows only the best beneficial course, with an omitted feminine noun such as state or act understood after the relative pronoun.
rows.anchor: والقربان كناية عن ملابسة مال اليتيم . والتصرف فيه كما تقدم آنفا في قوله : { ولا تقربوا الفواحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine relative can stand for an omitted state or act, as in the command to repel evil in the best manner and the fixed proverb after the lesser and greater calamity; Salmi's line illustrates the proverb.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى : { ادفع بالتي هي أحسن السيئة

rows.speaker: سلمي بن ربيعة الضبي
rows.claim: His verse uses the idiom اللتيا والتي for the lesser and greater calamities, illustrating the conventional feminine-relative construction.
rows.anchor:
كما قال سلمي بن ربيعة الضبي :
ولقد رأبت ثأى العشيرة بينها
وكفيت جانبها اللتيا والتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahsan means beneficial, not harmful to the orphan or the property; the command says do not approach, warning against even the slightest taking because the orphan cannot defend himself.
rows.anchor: اسم تفضيل مسلوب المفاضلة ، أي الحسنة ، وهي النافعة التي لا ضر فيها لليتيم ولا لماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order concerns trade: dates and raisins were sold by measure and gold and silver by weight, while traders shorted buyers to increase profit.
rows.anchor: وذلك في التبايع ، فقد كانوا يبيعون التمر والزبيب كيلا ، وكانوا يتوازنون الذهب والفضة ، فكانوا يطففون حرصا على الربح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The positive command to fulfill, unlike Shuayb's prohibition on reducing measures, focuses attention on doing justice and recalls Arabs' boast of generosity, exposing their moral inconsistency.
rows.anchor: وعدل عن أن يأتي فيه بالنهي عن التطفيف كما في قول شعيب : { ولا تنقصوا المكيال والميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition with fairness means to act justly and not deprive a customer of the amount due.
rows.anchor: أي أوفوا متلبسين بالعدل بأن لا تظلموا المكتال حقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The capacity clause qualifies exact measurement: people owe what they reasonably judge fair, not perfect accuracy to the smallest grain, so fear of error will not halt useful trade.
rows.anchor: لا نكلفكم تمام القسط في الكيل والميزان بالحبة والذرة ولكنا نكلفكم ما تظنون أنه عدل ووفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to God's direct first-person voice makes this qualification a special favor and confirms the messenger; fair measure protects buyers who are distracted while the seller controls the measure, so stronger forms of taking property are even more forbidden.
rows.anchor: فتولى الله خطاب الناس فيه بطريق التكلم مباشرة زيادة في المنة ، وتصديقا للمبلغ ، فالوصاية بإيفاء الكيل والميزان راجعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The capacity clause may qualify fair measures as requiring reasonable effort, or may summarize that all preceding duties lie within people's ability; the latter reading generalizes the point made at 2:286.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون جملة : { لا نكلف نفسا إلا وسعها } تذييلا للجمل التي قبلها ، تسجيلا عليهم بأن جميع ما دعوا إليه هو في طاقتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to speak justly covers all speech-mediated dealings: testimony, judgment, evaluations, advice, reconciliation, descriptions, promises, wills, oaths, praise, and insults or slander.
rows.anchor: هذا جامع كل المعاملات بين الناس بواسطة الكلام وهي الشهادة ، والقضاء ، والتعديل ، والتجريح ، والمشاورة ، والصلح بين الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Justice in speech means not violating rights: disclose defects, avoid invented defects or false prices, give honest evaluations and advice, speak truth in reconciliation and testimony, honor promises and inheritance rights, avoid false oaths, praise truthfully, and refrain from insults even if deserved.
rows.anchor: والعدل في ذلك أن لا يكون في القول شيء من الاعتداء على الحقوق : بإبطالها ، أو إخفائها ، مثل كتمان عيوب المبيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional wording leaves room for silence when one cannot speak justly, but no license to speak unjustly; some silence is itself obligatory.
rows.anchor: وفي التعليق بأداة الشرط في قوله : { وإذا قلتم } إشارة إلى أن المرء في سعة من السكوت إن خشي قول العدل

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: A report in the Muwatta says Umar struck or nearly struck a man who told a suitor that the man's sister had previously transgressed, then asked why he had shared the information.
rows.anchor: وفي ( الموطأ ) أن رجلا خطب إلى رجل أخته فذكر الأخ أنها قد كانت أحدثت فبلغ ذلك عمر بن الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw is circumstantial and law concessive, emphasizing even the exceptional case of kinship; the implied person discussed may be related to the speaker, whose bias must not displace justice.
rows.anchor: والواو في قوله : { ولو كان } واو الحال ، ولو وصلية تفيد المبالغة في الحال التي من شأنها أن يظن السامع عدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether speaking for or against a relative, one must not conceal a liability, invent a right, or absolve wrongdoing; the parallel rule for witness and judge appears at 4:135.
rows.anchor: إذا قلتم قولا لأجله أو عليه فاعدلوا ولا تقولوا غير الحق ، لا لدفع ضره بأن تغمصوا الحق الذي عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Positive command to make speech just better serves disclosure of truth than merely forbidding falsehood; it also avoids condemning indirect speech allowed under fear, accommodation, or circumstances where no right is at stake.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء طلب الحق في القول بصيغة الأمر بالعدل ، دون النهي عن الظلم أو الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says indirect expressions provide room to avoid lying, supporting the author's distinction between falsehood and permissible equivocal speech.
rows.anchor: وتلك هي المعاريض التي ورد فيها حديث : ( إن في المعاريض لمندوحة عن الكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's covenant may mean rules God imposed, a pledge people made to God, or any human covenant God commands them to keep; the genitive preserves all these senses.
rows.anchor: أن تكون إضافة المصدر إلى الفاعل ، أي ما عهد الله به إليكم من الشرائع ، ويصح أن تكون إضافة المصدر إلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the address is to polytheists, the covenant includes their known alliances and peace agreements; calling it God's covenant reflects their practice of swearing oaths when contracting.
rows.anchor: للمشركين تعين أن يكون العهد شيئا قد تقررت معرفته بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites الحارث بن حلزة’s verse as an example of Arabs praising fidelity to covenants.
rows.anchor:
واذكروا حلف ذي المجاز وما
قدم فيه العهود والكفلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites عمرو بن كلثوم’s verse as an example of Arabs praising fidelity to covenants.
rows.anchor:
وقال عمرو بن كلثوم :
ونوجد نحن أمنعهم ذمارا
وأوفاهم إذا عقدوا يمينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arab pacts against injustice in Mecca, including the Hilf al-Fudul and the Mutayyibin alliance, implemented God's promise to Abraham that Mecca be safe; persecuting vulnerable Muslims violated that safety and their own covenants.
rows.anchor: ومن العهود المقررة بينهم : حلف الفضول ، وحلف المطيبين ، وكلاهما كان في الجاهلية على نفي الظلم والجور عن القاطنين بمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant phrase is fronted to emphasize that fidelity to God's covenant matters most: if they prize keeping agreements, they should keep the covenant they chose, as in the contrast at 2:217.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المجرور على عامله للاهتمام بأمر العهد وصرف ذهن السامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated closing formula ends this class of rules; remembrance is apt because the four duties were recognized Arab virtues, but desire and idolatry had made them forget.
rows.anchor: وجاء مع هذه الوصية بقوله : { لعلكم تذكرون } لأن هذه المطالب الأربعة عرف بين العرب أنها محامد

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وأبو جعفر ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read tadhakkarun with doubled dhāl, assimilating the second tāʾ into the dhāl after changing it.
rows.anchor: نافع ، وابن كثير ، وأبو عمرو ، وابن عامر ، وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر ، وأبو جعفر ، ويعقوب : تذكرون بتشديد الذال

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وعاصم في رواية حفص وخلف
rows.claim: They read tadhakkarun with a light dhāl, deleting the second tāʾ for ease of pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة ، والكسائي ، وعاصم في رواية حفص ، وخلف بتخفيف الذال على حذف التاء الثانية تخفيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction links this command to the prohibition of associating partners in 6:151; its concluding exhortations parallel the sequence of purposes and affirm following Quranic revelation to the Messenger.
rows.anchor: الواو عاطفة على جملة : { ألا تشركوا به شيئا

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: They read anna with an open hamza and doubled nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع ، وابن كثير ، وأبو عمرو ، وعاصم ، وأبو جعفر : { أن } بفتح الهمزة وتشديد النون

rows.speaker: الفراء والكسائي
rows.claim: They attach anna to what the Lord prohibited in 6:151, making it an object of recitation: the Prophet is to recite that this is God's straight path.
rows.anchor: وعن الفراء والكسائي أنه معطوف على : { ما حرم ربكم

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Reporting Sibawayh's grammatical approach, he construes an omitted causal lām before anna: follow the path because it is straight, with the fronted reason functioning almost as a condition.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي علي الفارسي : أن قياس قول سيبويه أن تحمل ( أن ) ، أي تعلق على قوله : { فاتبعوه

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: They read inna with a closed hamza, preserving the order without ellipsis; following branches from the assertion that the path is straight.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة ، والكسائي ، وخلف : { وإن } بكسر الهمزة وتشديد النون فلا تحويل في نظم الكلام

rows.speaker: ابن عامر ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read anna open with a still nūn, either as a reduced emphatic particle with an implied subject pronoun, or preferably as explanatory and coordinated with the command not to associate partners; the repeated particle marks a change in style.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ، ويعقوب : ( وأن ) بفتح الهمزة وسكون النون على أنها مخففة من الثقيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of Pharaoh's threat, what the magicians would come to know, is omitted to make the threat terrifying; the definite plural covers every hand and foot of every sorcerer.
rows.anchor: وحذف مفعول { تعلمون } لقصد الإجمال في الوعيد لإدخال الرعب ، ثم بينه بجملة { لأقطعن أيديكم وأرجلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min khilaf identifies opposite sides: each sorcerer loses one hand and the opposite foot, leaving the person able to walk or lean on a stick.
rows.anchor: أنه يقطع من كل ساحر يدا ورجلا متخالفتي الجهة غير متقابلتيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If crucifixion means killing on a cross, the threat names two alternative punishments for different groups; cutting first then killing would make the crosswise detail pointless.
rows.anchor: موجه إلى جماعتهم فعلم أنه جعلهم فريقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, crucifixion may mean suspension without killing after amputation, as a public warning; then thumma signals a delay for healing, and all are crucified.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد بالصلب : الصلب دون قتل ، فيكون أراد صلبهم بعد القطع ليجعلهم نكالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians' reply that they return to God answers that Pharaoh's threat cannot harm them; they hope for God's reward and forgiveness and for punishment of Pharaoh, or welcome martyrdom and meeting God.
rows.anchor: وعيد لا يضيرهم ، لأنهم يعلمون أنهم صائرون إلى الله رب الجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say Pharaoh has no reason to punish them except their faith in the signs once they saw them.
rows.anchor: فإنك لا تعرف لنا سببا يوجب العقوبة غير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naqama means to object to an act, hate it, or resent its doer, by speech or action; it can follow two verb patterns, the first more eloquent, and all reciters use the form with a kasra on qāf.
rows.anchor: والنقم : بسكون القاف وبفتحها ، الإنكار على الفعل ، وكراهة صدوره وحقد على فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception for believing is connected: faith is precisely what Pharaoh resents, so it is not a seeming contradiction.
rows.anchor: والاستثناء في قولهم : { إلا أن آمنا بآيات ربنا } متصل ، لأن الإيمان ينقمه فرعون عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prayer turns from addressing Pharaoh to addressing God, asking for capacity to endure his threat; pouring patience pictures exceptional strength through a hidden vessel metaphor, imagined pouring, and an implication of filling completely.
rows.anchor: فشه الصبر بماء تشبيه المعقول بالمحسوس ، على طريقة الاستعارة المكنية ، وشبه خلقه في نفوسهم بإفراغ الماء من الإناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking to die as Muslims shows no desire for worldly life, confidence in the afterlife, and disregard for Pharaoh's threat; God may have spared them worldly disgrace, though the Quran omits the threat's fulfillment to emphasize God's support, their guidance, and steadfast faith.
rows.anchor: ودعوا لأنفسهم بالوفاة على الإسلام إيذانا بأنهم غير راغبين في الحياة ، ولا مبالين بوعيد فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The asylum clause may elaborate the repentance condition or qualify the command to kill polytheists: spare one who seeks access to conduct an embassy or learn Islam.
rows.anchor: لتفصيل مفهوم الشرط ، أو عطف على جملة { فاقتلوا المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional formula emphasizes the rule and anticipates a request for protection; إن presents a hypothetical, rare condition so polytheists cannot claim they lacked a chance to meet the Prophet and use that as an excuse for continued idolatry.
rows.anchor: وجيء بحرف { إن } التي شأنها أن يكون شرطها نادر الوقوع للتنبيه على أن هذا شرط فرضي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Razi transmits that a polytheist asked Ali whether they would be killed if they came after the deadline to hear the Quran or for another need; Ali answered no and cited this verse, but Ibn Ashur says he could not locate the report and notes it would have occurred after revelation.
rows.anchor: في ( تفسير الفخر ) أنه نقل عن ابن عباس قال : إن رجلا من المشركين قال لعلي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a conditional, the indefinite one could mean the whole class or some individuals; explicitly saying one of the polytheists specifies universal coverage, and ahad derives from wahid and denotes an individual person.
rows.anchor: وجيء بلفظ أحد من المشركين دون لفظ مشرك للتنصيص على عموم الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting one of the polytheists first focuses attention on the person seeking asylum before the request is mentioned.
rows.anchor: وتقديم { أحد } على { استجارك } للاهتمام بالمسند إليه ، ليكون أول ما يقرع السمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite noun may be initial because it is generic or because a conditional implies generality like a negation; a following verbal predicate licenses this order, and calling the noun an agent of an implied verb is only a grammatical interpretive device.
rows.anchor: ولذلك شاع عند النحاة أنه فاعل بفعل مقدر ، وإنما هو تقدير اعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Universality and fronting emphasize protection for any polytheist with a sound reason to visit, even someone from a tribe that broke its pact, lest Muslims answer betrayal with betrayal.
rows.anchor: تأكيد بذل الأمان لمن يسأله من المشركين إذا كان للقائه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ودخوله بلاد الإسلام مصلحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's rule forbids betraying someone who betrayed you, supporting the prohibition on retaliatory treachery.
rows.anchor: وقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( ولا تخن من خانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking neighboring protection became a common metaphor for seeking security, since residence requires safety; ajara means secure, not make someone a neighbor, and the purpose is left to reasonable motives.
rows.anchor: والاستجارة : طلب الجوار ، وهو الكون بالقرب ، وقد استعمل مجازا شائعا في الأمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether or not hearing the Quran was the visitor's original purpose, a temporary stay inevitably includes discussion and the Prophet's invitation to Islam; hearing God's speech marks the point when those purposes are complete.
rows.anchor: جعل سماع هذا المستجير القرآن غاية لإقامته الوقتية عند الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's speech means the Quran: God originated it to convey His intent and sent it through an angel to the Prophet, rather than a human composing it as with a hadith qudsi.
rows.anchor: وكلام الله : القرآن ، أضيف إلى اسم الجلالة لأنه كلام أوجده الله ليدل على مراده من الناس وأبلغه إلى الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma stresses the higher-priority duty to keep the visitor protected in Muslim territory until he reaches safety, even if that takes a long time.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على وجوب استمرار إجارته في أرض الإسلام إلى أن يبلغ المكان الذي يأمن فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To deliver him to safety means let him go and do not harm him until he reaches safety; it does not require the Prophet to arrange an escort or transport.
rows.anchor: أمهله ولا تهجه حتى يبلغ مأمنه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: When a student asked permission to swallow his saliva, his teacher replied that he had granted him the Tigris and Euphrates, illustrating the idiom for asking someone to wait.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري : قلت لبعض أشياخي : ( أبلعني ريقي فقال قد أبلعتك الرافدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma'man means the visitor's own place of safety, normally his home territory, distinguished from temporary asylum by the possessive pronoun.
rows.anchor: مكان الأمن ، وهو المكان الذي يجد فيه المستجير أمنه السابق ، وذلك هو دار قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause explains the whole command: protect the asylum seeker despite past harm until home because he does not know Quranic guidance; the wording both condemns his ignorance and explains the accommodation.
rows.anchor: فالإشارة إلى مضمون جملة : { فأجره حتى يسمع كلام الله ثم أبلغه مأمنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Provision from heaven is rain, and provision from earth is all vegetation, including grain, fruit, and pasture.
rows.anchor: فالرزق من السماء المطر ، والرزق من الأرض النبات كله من حب وثمر وكلأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Am marks a transition to another question; God's ownership of hearing and sight means control over their creation, recalling the useful and subtle creation of these faculties.
rows.anchor: ومعنى : { يملك السمع والأبصار } يملك التصرف فيهما ، وهو ملك إيجاد تينك الحاستين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing is a singular verbal noun that denotes the species collectively; sight is plural to make universal intent explicit and avoid a possible reference to one particular sight, unlike the individual faculties addressed in 17:36.
rows.anchor: وأفرد { السمع } لأنه مصدر فهو دال على الجنس الموجود في جميع حواس الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life emerging from death includes animal offspring from initially lifeless sperm or eggs as they develop; death emerging from life means sperm or eggs produced by animals. The definite terms mean the species.
rows.anchor: هو تولد أطفال الحيوان من النطف ومن البيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciprocal creation is phrased as a riddle with antithesis to heighten wonder; unlike the similar passage in 3:27, this one carries no allusion to anything hidden.
rows.anchor: وقد نظم هذا الاستدلال على ذلك الصنع العجيب بأسلوب الأحاجي والألغاز وجعل بمحسن التضاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question who directs affairs generalizes after the specific signs in human beings, like the appeal to observe oneself and the heavens in 51:21–22.
rows.anchor: وهو هنا تعميم بعد تخصيص ذكر ما فيه مزيد عبرة في أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first fa treats the Prophet's command to ask as a condition: if he asks who provides and creates, the polytheists will say God; compare the same construction at 17:51–52.
rows.anchor: فنزل فعل { قل } منزلة الشرط فكأنه قيل : إن تقل من يرزقكم من السماء والأرض فسيقولون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians explain command constructions with a supplied conditional; the author says this is close to the more semantic analysis that treats the command itself as a condition, differing mainly in whether the estimate is grammatical or interpretive.
rows.anchor: والرأيان متقاربان إلا أن ما سلكه المحققون تقدير معنى والتقدير عندهم اعتبار لا استعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without treating the command as a condition, the fa would not appear, as in the distinct question-and-answer construction at 23:84–85.
rows.anchor: ولو لم ينزل الأمر بمنزلة الشرط لما جاءت الفاء كما في قوله تعالى : { قل لمن الأرض ومن فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa in then say is explanatory: if they answer, ask whether they will not fear God by rejecting partners; the fa in the final question draws that rebuke from their admission.
rows.anchor: والفاء في قوله : { فقل } فاء الفصيحة ، أي إن قالوا ذلك فقل أفلا تتقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of fear is omitted but understood as God; the polytheists already acknowledged God alone as provider, creator, and director in many Quranic passages, and their inability to deny this truth leaves them convicted.
rows.anchor: وإنما أخبر الله عنهم بأنهم سيعترفون بأن الرازق والخالق والمدبر هو الله لأنهم لم يكونوا يعتقدون غير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening fa draws a conclusion from the rebuke in 10:31; the demonstrative gathers God's preceding qualities as grounds for the judgment, while naming Allah clarifies it and exposes the polytheists' error.
rows.anchor: واسم الإشارة عائد إلى اسم الجلالة للتنبيه على أن المشار إليه جدير بالحكم الذي سيذكر بعد اسم الإشارة من أجل الأوصاف المتقدمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following question's fa draws an emphatic, reproachful inference from the proof that God is true Lord; ma dha combines an interrogative with a demonstrative, usually for emphasis, though it can be relative elsewhere.
rows.anchor: والفاء في قوله : { فماذا بعد الحق إلا الضلال } تفريع للاستفهام الإنكاري على الاستنتاج الواقع بعد الدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After means other than what follows when truth is absent; the rhetorical question denies any middle way, so worship attributed to anything but the true Lord is false and aptly called error.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى لا يكون إثر انتفاء الحق إلا الضلال إذ لا واسطة بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa in where are you turned adds explicit rebuke after the denial; anna asks metaphorically where the listeners' reasoning leads them, as if they wandered from one false path to another.
rows.anchor: أي أنكم في ضلال وعماية كمن ضل عن الطريق ولا يجد إلا من ينعت له طريقا غير موصلة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He praises the Quran's way of expressing these meanings as surpassing every explanation in eloquence, brevity, and clarity.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية : وعبارة القرآن في سوق هذه المعاني تفوق كل تفسير براعة وإيجازا ووضوحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage contains nine fa particles: the first is a response, the second explanatory, and all remaining ones mark consequences.
rows.anchor: وقد اشتملت هذه الآيات على تسع فاءات من قوله : { فسيقولون الله } : الأولى جوابية ، والثانية فصيحة ، والبواقي تفريعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a new sentence, and its demonstrative reinforces the preceding one in 11:18; the relative clause describes the known class who lost their own selves by failing to benefit from guidance.
rows.anchor: استئناف ، واسم الإشارة هنا تأكيد ثان لاسم الإشارة في قوله : { أولئك يعرضون على ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their invented claims were that idols could intercede or avert hardship; attributing straying to idols mocks their worshipers by picturing the idols losing their way to those who sought help.
rows.anchor: ما كانوا يزعمونه من أن الأصنام تشفع لهم وتدفع عنهم الضر عند الشدائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final sentence summarizes the preceding exposure, punishment, refusal to hear warnings, and neglect of monotheistic evidence, all of which establish their loss in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: فذلكة ونتيجة للجمل المتقدمة من قوله : { أولئك يعرضون على ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La jarama is an idiom of certainty; Ibn Ashur regards jarama as a fossilized noun meaning inevitably or without alternative, with an omitted preposition governing anna, and the phrase can introduce an oath-like assertion.
rows.anchor: اسم بمعنى محالة أي لا محالة أو بمعنى بد أي لا بد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling their harm a loss is a metaphor: like traders they suffered damage while expecting benefit.
rows.anchor: وعبر عما لحقهم من الضر بالخسارة استعارة لأنه ضر أصابهم من حيث كانوا يرجون المنفعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are the greatest losers because they combine the forms of misery and punishment scattered among deluded nations, and were miserable precisely where they expected happiness, losing both this world and the next.
rows.anchor: ولأنهم شقوا من حيث كانوا يحسبونه سعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separating pronoun restricts the judgment rhetorically: they reached the greatest possible loss, as though no one else shared that distinction.
rows.anchor: وضمير { هم الأخسرون } ضمير فصل يفيد القصر ، وهو قصر ادعائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase on his shirt is a circumstantial phrase belonging to blood, placed before its head noun.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { على قميصه } حال من ( دم ) فقدم على صاحب الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal rejects the brothers' claim that a wolf ate Joseph and explicitly calls their story false; taswila means making attractive what the self wants to obtain.
rows.anchor: حرف الإضراب إبطال لدعواهم أن الذئب أكله فقد صرح لهم بكذبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vague matter could have been killing, selling, or banishing Joseph; its indefinite form makes their act sound ominous.
rows.anchor: والإبهام الذي في كلمة { أمرا } يحتمل عدة أشياء مما يمكن أن يؤذوا به يوسف عليه السلام : من قتل ، أو بيع ، أو تغريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beautiful patience stands for a command to be patient; its nominative form conveys firmness and duration, and may be an aside to the sons, a self-address, or an elliptical statement of Jacob's affair, with the exhortative reading strongest.
rows.anchor: عدل به عن النصب إلى الرفع للدلالة على الثبات والدوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim ibn Kunyaf al-Nahshali's poem says patience is more beautiful for a free person than there being no reliance against time, illustrating a possible descriptive use of beautiful.
rows.anchor:
كما قال إبراهيم بن كنيف النبهاني :
تصبر فإن الصبر بالحر أجمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beautiful may specify patience free from agitation, rather than merely explain that patience is good; its beauty is the most excellent, unblemished state of patience.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون وصفا مخصصا . وقد فسر الصبر الجميل بالذي لا يخالطه جزع

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In an author-described sound hadith, the Prophet told a grieving woman to fear God and be patient; after learning who he was, she returned, and he said complete patience is at the first shock.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح أن النبي عليه السلام مر بامرأة تبكي عند قبر فقال لها : ( اتقي الله واصبري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob's statement about God as the one sought for help may be a prayer for aid or a report that he relies on God to endure, and may also ask God to free Joseph.
rows.anchor: فتكون محتملة للمعنيين المذكورين من إنشاء الاستعانة أو الإخبار بحصول استعانته بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What you describe is deliberately open-ended: Jacob knows his sons are lying and harmed Joseph but not exactly how; they mean the wolf's supposed killing, while Jacob means the actual injury, resembling 37:180.
rows.anchor: لأنه كان واثقا بأنهم كاذبون في الصفة وواثقا بأنهم ألحقوا بيوسف عليه السلام ضرا فلما لم يتعين عنده المصاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob leaves the matter to God because old age and lack of allies make him unable to uncover Joseph's fate without his sons; once he has an opportunity, he tells them to search for Joseph and his brother.
rows.anchor: ولأنه لا عضد له يستعين به على أبنائه أولئك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God's blessings cannot be counted reinforces and broadens the preceding conclusion: many blessings are known, and many cannot be comprehended or are forgotten when people try to count them.
rows.anchor: تنبيها على أن ما آتاهم الله كثير منه معلوم وكثير منه لا يحيطون بعلمه أو لا يتذكرونه عند إرادة تعداد النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Counting means attempting enumeration; familiar but overlooked blessings include breathing, senses, digestion, circulation, and health. Ibn al-Fakhr has a valuable discussion on this point.
rows.anchor: وذلك مثل النعم المعتاد بها التي ينسى الناس أنها من النعم ، كنعمة التنفس ، ونعمة الحواس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihsa means accurately fixing a number and derives from pebbles, which people once used to count large totals without error.
rows.anchor:
والإحصاء : ضبط العدد
 ، وهو مشتق من الحصا اسما للعدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing assertion reinforces the rebuke of turning blessings into disbelief; human here means the polytheist, as elsewhere in the Quran.
rows.anchor: صنف منه ، وهو المتصف بمضمون الجملة المؤكدة وتأكيدها ، فالإنسان هو المشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensive forms reflect the abundance of blessings and corresponding ingratitude: idolaters abandon worship of the giver for powerless objects, whereas believers acknowledge God's gifts and worship no other.
rows.anchor: إذ بمقدار كثرة النعم يكثر كفر الكافرين بها إذ أعرضوا عن عبادة المنعم وعبدوا ما لا يغني عنهم شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is an admonition to believers: the wealth and children of polytheists are only temporary worldly adornment, while what God prepared for believers is better in reward and hope; see the warning about unbelievers' brief enjoyment.
rows.anchor: اعتراض أريد به الموعظة والعبرة للمؤمنين بأن ما فيه المشركون من النعمة من مال وبنين ما هو إلا زينة الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: طرفة
rows.claim: His poem reflects the well-known Arab pride in wealth and children, imagining having abundant property and noble sons.
rows.anchor:
قال طرفة :
فلو شاء ربي كنت قيس بن عاصم
ولو شاء ربي كنت عمرو بن مرثد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abiding righteous things are good deeds with lasting reward, therefore better than transient worldly adornment.
rows.anchor: الصالحات } صفتان جرتا على موصوف محذوف ، أي الأعمال الصالحات الباقيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expected order would be righteous before abiding, since righteous deeds is the familiar expression and permanence follows from goodness; righteous can stand as a noun for good works, as in the Quran and a line by Jarir.
rows.anchor: لأنهما وإن كانا وصفين لموصوف محذوف إلا أن أعرفهما في وصفية ذلك المحذوف هو الصالحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order is reversed to stress that wealth and children do not last, compressing the omitted statement that they vanish; the wind-scattered plant in 18:45 indicates this by representation, and abiding adds a reinforcing implication.
rows.anchor: فقدم ( الباقيات ) للتنبيه على أن ما ذكر قبله إنما كان مفصولا لأنه ليس
